title: Tidewell
summary: Tide and swell forecasts drawn as one continuous chart you scrub with your thumb.
description: Most surf apps give you a table of numbers per hour. Tidewell draws the next seven days as a single line — tide height, swell and wind layered on one axis — and lets you drag through time with your thumb. The whole forecast is cached for offline use, because the beach is exactly where the signal disappears.
highlights: Canvas-rendered chart holding 60fps while scrubbing 2,000+ data points
Offline-first: forecasts cached by a service worker, refreshed in the background
Haptic ticks on each hour mark on supported devices
coverAlt: Tidewell forecast chart with layered tide and swell lines

title: Kiln Studio
summary: A storefront for a two-person ceramics studio, with every piece on a real-time turntable.
description: Handmade ceramics sell on texture and glaze, which flat photos flatten. Each product on Kiln is a photogrammetry scan on a WebGL turntable you can spin and light yourself, with a still-photo fallback for low-power devices. The catalogue is small, so the whole shop is statically generated and loads before you finish scrolling.
highlights: Compressed scans averaging 480 KB each (Draco + KTX2)
Automatic fallback to photography on low-end GPUs
Checkout through the Shopify Storefront API — no page reloads
coverAlt: A glazed ceramic bowl on a turntable

title: Fieldwork Type
summary: A specimen site where every variable axis of the typeface is a slider you can grab.
description: Type foundries mostly sell with static specimens. For Fieldwork, every axis of the variable font — weight, width, optical size — is exposed as a live control, and the specimen pages respond to scroll by sweeping through them. It is a catalogue that doubles as a playground, built to stay fast with six font files in play.
highlights: Scroll-driven axis animation, scrubbed with ScrollTrigger
Font subsetting cut specimen payload by 71%
Tester text persists across pages in the session
coverAlt: Large letterforms from the Fieldwork typeface

title: Transit Pulse
summary: Live bus positions for a whole city, drawn as a single breathing map.
description: Transit Pulse streams vehicle positions over WebSockets and interpolates between updates, so buses glide instead of jumping every thirty seconds. Routes that run late slowly warm in colour. Built in a weekend, then kept alive for a year because people actually used it at bus stops.
highlights: Handles 1,200 live vehicles on a mid-range phone
Colour scale checked for colour-blind legibility
coverAlt: City map with bus routes drawn as lines

gallery.alt: Route lines over the city grid

title: Margin Notes
summary: A reading app that turns your highlights into spaced-repetition cards.
description: You highlight a sentence; a week later Margin Notes asks you about it. Everything lives in IndexedDB on your device — no account, no sync server — and the review queue is scheduled with a simplified SM-2 algorithm. The interface is deliberately quiet: one card, one question, one tap.
highlights: Local-first: all data in IndexedDB, exportable as Markdown
Fully keyboard operable, tested with VoiceOver
coverAlt: A review card with a highlighted sentence

title: Salt & Signal
summary: A home for a coastal-radio podcast, with a waveform that listens back.
description: The site for Salt & Signal is built around its player: the waveform is drawn from the actual audio via the Web Audio API and reacts to the episode as it plays. Episode pages load instantly from a static build and resume where you left off, even across devices on the same browser profile.
highlights: Real-time waveform from an AnalyserNode, drawn on canvas
Transcripts synced to the audio, clickable to seek
coverAlt: Audio waveform over a sea-blue field
